A Tribute to Mrs. Simone Tata Chairperson Emeritus 2 nd March 1930 – 5 th December 2025 We honour and celebrate the remarkable life and legacy of Mrs. Simone Tata, Chairperson Emeritus of Trent, whose vision and leadership have left an enduring mark on the organisation. Mrs. Tata’s exceptional understanding of fashion, style, and consumer behaviour reshaped the retail experience in India. With the opening of the first Westside store in Bengaluru, she brought to life a thoughtful vision of creating a brand that offered refined and meaningful lifestyle choices to Indian households. Her clarity of purpose and commitment to excellence continue to shape Trent’s approach to quality, design, and customer experience. Beyond her professional accomplishments, Mrs. Tata was deeply committed to making a difference in society. Her contributions to philanthropic initiatives, particularly in supporting women and children, reflect her compassion and sense of responsibility. Mrs.

Tata’s legacy lives on through the values she championed and the strong foundation she built. Her vision continues to inspire and guide Trent as it carries forward the foundation she so thoughtfully built. We remember and celebrate her with deep respect and gratitude. Mrs. Tata It’s all so new, they kept saying. It is the future, I kept insisting.

Reporting Approach This Report presents a comprehensive and integrated overview of Trent Limited’s (‘the Company’ or ‘Trent’) performance and value creation journey. It brings together financial and non-financial information to provide stakeholders with meaningful insights into the Company’s business strategy, operating environment, governance framework, key priorities, risk landscape, sustainability initiatives, as well as its approach to creating long-term value for all its stakeholders. Frameworks, Guidelines and Standards This Report is guided by the principles of the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC) Framework.

The statutory reports, including the Board’s Report Management Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) Corporate Governance Report Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements, are in line with the applicable Indian Accounting Standards, the Companies Act, 2013, Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and the Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. Forward-Looking Statements This Report contains certain forward- looking statements concerning our business operations, financial position, strategy, objectives, and future performance. These statements are based on current assumptions and expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and evolving business conditions. While we believe the assumptions are reasonable, actual outcomes may differ materially.

The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update forward- looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise, except as required by the applicable laws and regulations. Feedback We value stakeholder engagement and welcome your feedback on our performance and reporting. For queries or suggestions, please contact: BDO India Services Private Limited has provided reasonable assurance on the non-financial disclosures included in BRSR Report (BRSR Core) for the reporting period, in accordance with the International Standards on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) and International Standards on Assurance Engagements 3410 standards, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). Scope and Reporting Boundary This Report covers the standalone and consolidated financial performance of Trent, including its subsidiaries, associate and group companies, for the financial year from 1 st April 2025 to 31 st March 2026.

The standalone and consolidated financial statements have been audited by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, Chartered Accountants. Non-financial information has been reported primarily on a standalone basis for Trent. Given the materiality and future growth agenda, select coverage of our food business under the Star banner has also been included. A s I look back at Trent’s journey, I am filled with a deep sense of reflection. What started as a thoughtful transition from Lakmé into an emerging fashion retail space has, over time, become something ever more meaningful. On a personal note, I often reflect on the early conversations I had with my mother, Mrs. Simone Tata, when we were considering the transition of Lakmé into a new direction. At the heart of those discussions was a simple but powerful aspiration - to create products and experiences that people truly love and desire and yet rooted in Tata values. It is deeply satisfying to see that, in many ways, this aspiration has come to fruition through Trent’s progress over the past two and a half decades. In 1998, when we began with a single Westside store at Commercial Street in Bengaluru, modern fashion retail in India was almost non-existent. The idea of creating a contemporary, accessible retail experience for Indian consumers was both ambitious and uncertain.

Yet, it was also energising - because we were not just building a business, we were participating in shaping a new business category in the country. More than 25 years later, the transformation has been extraordinary - first and foremost for India itself. The India we operate in today is vastly different. There is a greater exposure to global trends, rising aspirations across demographics, and an increasing ability among consumers to pursue lifestyle choices. The growth in disposable incomes and the desire for self-expression through fashion have fundamentally reshaped consumption patterns. We have witnessed a remarkable evolution - not only in people’s sense of fashion, but also in how they think, choose, and live. The proliferation of choice, the openness to change, and the confidence of the Indian consumer have all contributed to creating a vibrant and competitive marketplace.

Through all these changes, I am extremely proud that Trent has remained grounded and anchored firmly in the values of the Tata group. Even as the environment became more Dear Shareholders, dynamic and competitive, and even as consumer expectations underwent dramatic shifts, our focus on delivering genuine customer value has remained unwavering. From a single Westside store to a network of over twelve hundred stores, our journey has been one of steady evolution. Over the years, we have added powerful growth engines to our portfolio - most notably Zudio and Star - which are now a significant part of our portfolio. The strength of Trent today lies not just in scale, but in the diversity and relevance of our brands. We have also worked towards building an integrated ecosystem - across design, sourcing, supply chain, and retail execution - to ensure that each of our brands delivers a differentiated and compelling customer experience.

This ability to combine back-end strength with front-end innovation has been central to our progress. I have long believed that Trent is not intended to be defined by a single brand, but rather by a portfolio of brands. In a diverse and evolving market like India as well as globally, it is unlikely that any one brand can capture a dominant share of the lifestyle space. Instead, our approach has been to create distinct, well-defined propositions that cater to different customer needs and occasions. This multi-brand strategy will continue to guide our future. As we look ahead, I firmly believe that the best years of Trent are ahead of us. The opportunities before us are vast - not just in India. In the years to come, I see Trent touching even more lives through our offerings, expanding across categories, and exploring new geographies over time. It would be enormously satisfying to shape and build brands from India that go on to be globally relevant in diverse markets.

Further, as we consider this future, we should also aspire for material scale of revenues from overseas markets. This would be completely in line with the national agenda of growing value added exports from our country. We should aspire boldly, execute with perseverance and celebrate the pride of brands - built ground up from India! As we move forward, our journey will remain deeply collaborative. Our stakeholders - our employees, partners, suppliers, communities, and shareholders - are integral to everything we do. Together, we will continue to build a responsible, sustainable, and meaningful business of scale. Given the significant opportunities that remain ahead and the growing strength of Trent’s platform, I believe we are still at an early phase of our growth journey. With a strong ecosystem around us and a clear sense of purpose, we are positioned to build upon this platform.

In our 2023 shareholders meeting, I had envisioned Trent to be ten times bigger in terms of revenues with commensurate profitability. Since then, the revenue and profitability run rate has grown by over 2.5 times. Given all this, I am confident that we will reach the milestone I had referenced in the not-so-distant future. I sincerely thank you for your continued trust in Trent and for being an integral part of our journey. NOEL N. Letter from the Managing Director F Y26 marked another year of meaningful progress for Trent, driven by a portfolio anchored in customer relevance, strong value propositions, and long-term engagement. Our core fashion brands - Westside and Zudio - continued to deliver strong, complementary growth across segments. We are also encouraged by the early momentum with Burnt Toast, our new lifestyle brand proposition that appeals to trend-forward and Gen-Z consumers. Our food and grocery business, Star continues to evolve in a significant way, building on the Trent playbook. The year saw substantial interventions with respect to the operating model with a refreshed emphasis on in-store customer experience. We remain encouraged by the traction that our own brand propositions are witnessing across micro markets. Own brands now contribute to 73% of Star’s revenues and remain the core differentiating proposition of the brand.

We continue to pursue a disciplined expansion program that is aimed at growing share of presence in existing micro markets as well as establishing reach to numerous new cities and towns across India. This growth has been supported by a more robust operating backbone, enabling quicker turnarounds, faster refresh cycles, and improved execution at scale. Alongside footprint expansion, we maintained a strong focus on financial discipline - optimising store-level margins and leveraging digital platforms to strengthen our omni-channel connect. Our teams remain central to execution in a relatively challenging macroeconomic context, driving productivity improvements across multiple areas and reinforcing a culture of pursuing excellence. Technology and digital initiatives remained key enablers for Trent during the year.

We continued to strengthen our digital ecosystem by investing in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, and automation to enhance product design, merchandise planning, improve supply chain efficiency, and elevate in-store and omni-channel customer experiences. AI-led use cases are increasingly supporting demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, and delivery of a more customer-relevant engagement across channels. Dear Shareholders, As we look ahead, we do so with confidence and an unwavering commitment to serve our customers better every day. To our colleagues, partners, and shareholders - thank you for your trust and support. We remain energised by the opportunity ahead and are determined to build a future-ready Trent that creates enduring value. P.

Governance that Reinforces Trust Board Composition The Board consists of seven Directors, of whom four are Independent Directors, representing 57.1% of its composition (including 2 women directors constituting 28.6%). The remaining members include two Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors, including the Chairman, besides the Managing Director. We lead with integrity, accountability, and transparency as core values rooted in the Tata ethos. This shapes how we manage risk, allocate capital, and engage with stakeholders to create consistent, long-term value. Governance Structure Our governance framework is designed to promote accountability and informed decision-making across the organisation. It is guided by the Tata Code of Conduct and our internal policies. All employees are expected to follow Trent’s values and act with honesty, fairness, and integrity. We follow a structured and inclusive approach to decision-making to ensure consistency and transparency.

All decisions are aligned with the Company’s overall objectives and long-term strategy, supporting sustainable growth. This approach also strengthens governance practices and enhances overall organisational effectiveness. The structure operates through multiple tiers: the Board of Directors, Board Committees, the Managing Director and the Leadership Team. The Board brings together members with extensive business experience and strong credibility across sectors. Their diverse expertise and independent perspectives strengthen deliberations. The Board acts in good faith, with due diligence, care and in the best interests of the shareholders. Board Committees form an integral part of this framework. They are delegated specific responsibilities by the Board.

These Committees provide focused oversight and guidance across key areas such as audit, risk management, nomination and remuneration, stakeholder relations, governance, CSR, and sustainability, enhancing the Board’s ability to discharge its responsibilities thoroughly and efficiently. The Managing Director and the Leadership Team lead strategy and drive execution, ensuring operational excellence and sustained growth.

These updates enable informed oversight and decision-making. Effective Governance and Ethical Practices Governance The Company is committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics, transparency, and fairness in all its dealings. Its governance framework is anchored in the Tata Code of Conduct, which promotes responsible behaviour across the organisation. The Company has implemented a robust Whistle Blower Policy and Vigil Mechanism to promote a transparent and safe working environment. Employees and stakeholders can report concerns through confidential channels, including an independent ethics helpline and secure email mechanisms, without fear of retaliation. All grievances, including those relating to human rights and the prevention of sexual harassment, are addressed through a structured redressal process. The Company maintains a zero-tolerance approach towards unethical practices and remains committed to safeguarding the rights and dignity of all stakeholders.

Disclosures The Company complies with all applicable statutory and regulatory disclosures well within the prescribed timelines. This includes financial reporting, regulatory filings, ESG disclosures, and timely disclosure of material events, ensuring accuracy and completeness in public communication. Data Privacy The Company’s Information Security Policy provides a structured approach to managing information assets through a multi-layered framework of organisational, physical, and technological controls. An Information Security Management System (ISMS), led by the Chief Technology Officer, supports proactive risk management, regulatory compliance, and periodic reviews. A defined Incident Management Policy, along with a Cyber Crisis Response Plan, enables effective identification and mitigation of security risks.

Regular security audits, cyber maturity assessments, and employee awareness programmes help strengthen a culture of vigilance and preparedness, in alignment with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Internal Controls The Company maintains an adequate and effective internal financial control framework to safeguard its assets and ensure efficient operations. The framework is supported by documented policies, procedures, and process guidelines across key functions. Regular review of the risk and control matrix enables the strengthening of preventive and automated controls and timely mitigation of risks. The internal control system provides reasonable assurance on the reliability of financial reporting, compliance with applicable laws, and operational effectiveness. It is subject to continuous monitoring and periodic review to ensure its ongoing adequacy and effectiveness.

The Company has also established defined frameworks governing related party transactions and the prevention of insider trading, supported by clear oversight and review mechanisms. Risk Management Framework The Company follows an Enterprise Risk Management (‘ERM’) approach that is integrated with strategy planning and performance management processes. It has adopted the COSO (Committee of Sponsoring Organisations of the Treadway Commission), 2017 ERM framework in this context. Integrating ERM practices aligned with the COSO framework across the organisation enhances performance by linking strategy and business objectives with risk-assessed decision-making and cultivates an appropriate risk management culture. Vendor Governance Supplier selection and evaluation are aligned with the SMETA four-pillar framework, covering labour standards, health and safety, environmental practices, and business ethics. This approach supports the development of a responsible and resilient supply chain.
The Vendor Code of Conduct sets standards for ethical, compliant, and responsible practices across our supply chain.

Industry Dynamics and Market Environment India remains one of the fastest-growing major economies, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals and ongoing reforms. Rising incomes, urbanization, and evolving consumer preferences continue to drive consumption-led growth, creating significant opportunities for the retail sector. India is poised to become the third-largest economy with USD 7.3 Trillion GDP by 2030 1 , reflecting its expanding role and influence in the global economy. Rising Middle Class and Aspirational Consumption A rapidly expanding middle-income population, supported by rising earning capacity, is driving discretionary spending across lifestyle categories such as fashion, accessories, and consumer goods. As purchasing power strengthens, consumers increasingly move beyond basic purchases toward branded and value-driven offerings, supporting growth in organised retail formats.

Growing Demand from Tier II and Tier III Markets Consumption growth in emerging cities is becoming a key driver of retail expansion. Rising aspirations and improving local incomes are increasing acceptance of branded merchandise, enabling organised retailers to deepen market penetration beyond metropolitan regions and widen access to quality products. Urbanisation Supporting Modern Retail Expansion Continued urban migration is transforming cities into consumption hubs, increasing demand for malls and integrated retail destinations. Shopping spaces are evolving into lifestyle centres that combine retail, entertainment, and dining, encouraging longer customer engagement and higher in-store spending. Strengthening Organised Retail Regulatory reforms and the government push to drive economic growth have simplified compliance and improved supply chain efficiency, enabling greater transparency and faster inventory movement.

Alongside this, policy reforms such as easier approvals, improved ease of doing business, and supportive investment policies are strengthening retail infrastructure. The expansion of logistics networks, warehouses, and commercial spaces is helping organised retailers scale efficiently and enter underserved markets. Digital Acceleration and Phygital Retail Technology adoption is reshaping consumer journeys by integrating online discovery with offline fulfilment. Digital platforms and personalised engagement tools improve convenience and conversion, while phygital retail models combine e-commerce reach with the trust of physical stores through unified experiences and flexible fulfilment options. Advancements in Logistics and Fulfilment Capabilities The emergence of micro-fulfilment centres, modern warehousing, and just-in-time inventory systems are enhancing supply chain agility.

These advancements enable faster replenishment, improved availability, and cost efficiencies, allowing retailers to respond effectively to dynamic consumer demand. Preference for Experience-Led and Value Fashion Retail Modern shoppers increasingly seek engaging environments that blend convenience with inspiration. Experience-focused destinations and value fashion offerings that balance quality, design, and affordability are gaining strong traction among price-conscious yet brand-aware consumers. 1 Boston Consulting Group and Retailers Association of India - 2026 Report 49 48 Trent Limited Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Company Overview / Statutory Reports / Financial Statements / Notice

Risk Management Risk Governance The Risk Management Committee, the Audit Committee, and the Board review periodic updates on key enterprise risks and material changes in the Company’s risk profile, ensuring effective oversight at the highest levels. The execution of the risk management framework is driven by a central Risk Management function under the leadership of the Chief Financial Officer, enabling a consistent and coordinated approach across the organisation. The Company has adopted the COSO 2017 Enterprise Risk Management Framework for driving its risk management agenda. Ongoing communication initiatives and structured risk workshops promote awareness, accountability, and transparency in risk reporting. The use of technology and advanced analytics supports efficient, accurate, and timely monitoring of risks. Our structured Enterprise Risk Management framework, aligned with the COSO 2017 framework, provides effective oversight across governance, strategy, and business operations.

This integrated approach embeds risk considerations into strategic and operational decisions, reinforcing resilience, protecting value, and promoting a culture of disciplined decision-making. Risk Management Process Assess Risk Response Regular reviews and structured discussions enable risk owners and management to reassess exposure levels, evaluate the effectiveness of mitigation plans and undertake corrective actions. Develop Risk Response Mitigation strategies are structured around defined risk appetite and tolerance thresholds, with actions calibrated through risk acceptance, reduction, sharing or transfer, as appropriate. Monitor, Communicate and Report The management and leadership team engages on a regular basis to review the Company’s risk profile and evaluate the effectiveness of the risk management framework.

Identify and Analyse Risks are systematically identified and assessed across each business and support function along with an enterprise-wide, top-down perspective provided by the Board, the Audit Committee, and the Risk Management Committee. Assess and Prioritise Each identified risk is evaluated across impact, likelihood, and velocity, with due consideration to strategic priorities and operational deliverables. Key Market Risks and Mitigation Plan Geopolitical risks, such as wars, conflicts, and sanctions, can disrupt trade, investment, and financial stability, leading to economic downturns and fluctuations in asset prices. Conversely, macroeconomic risks encompass broader economic factors that can affect the economy’s performance, such as inflation, interest rates, and economic growth. We continuously monitor and reduce reliance on volatile trade routes and proactively prepare for regional disruptions. Maintaining liquidity buffers ensures minimal disruption and stable operations.

Navigating through regional restrictions and adapting through quick and effective responses has helped us build long-term resilience and deliver sustained growth. Macro Environmental Risk Trend relevance is central to our business. Any inability to anticipate or respond swiftly to evolving fashion preferences and changing consumer expectations poses a direct risk. Intensifying competition, the growing attractiveness of the sector and rapid technological innovation further heighten market complexity. At the same time, curating retail spaces, assortments and displays across diverse micro-markets and demographic segments adds executional challenges. Misalignment on these dimensions can materially impact consumer outcomes and delivered margins. Continuous monitoring of the market and competitive landscape, combined with active customer engagement, enables early identification of evolving needs and changes in the fashion trends.

Ongoing efforts to spot emerging fashion trends are reinforced by strong in-house design capabilities, supported by design studios in India and Spain, ensuring a refreshed and relevant product portfolio. Systematic identification and incubation of growth drivers and enablers support sustained business performance. Space management algorithms are calibrated to reflect regional and local variations, enhancing relevance and productivity across markets. A disciplined focus on margins, cost efficiency, quality, and compliance underpins a sustainable operating model aligned with changing consumer expectations. Resiliency for Trent is all about being relevant over time to a growing critical mass of customers in the lifestyle space. It is about the relative desirability of respective brand propositions in an otherwise crowded and competitive market place. At the next level, resilience should translate to relatively consistent performance across cycles notwithstanding a rapidly evolving consumer and competitive context. Performance outcomes should encompass growing revenues and customer base, strong unit economics, overall profitability and capital efficiencies. Also, a resilient business should importantly afford the trial, incubation and build out of additional growth engines (brands/ categories/ geographies) over time. How are we managing this: Own brands Our business model choices are at the core of delivering desirable customer propositions. The emphasis is on our own brands and nimble responsiveness to emerging consumer preferences.

The pursuit with each of our brands is for distinctive market positioning that is differentiated. Strong product disciplines including ownership of product design and curation, focus on speed of concept to market and consistency of offer across channels, are a defining feature of our playbook. Direct to consumer Trent is quintessentially direct-to- consumer as we adopt direct distribution and eschew third-party channels and intermediation of any kind. We focus on being accessible with the ubiquitous presence of our Trent’s digital advantage comes from what it owns and operates - its supply chain, brands, and distribution network of over 1,250 stores. Together, these generate proprietary, first-hand data across the value chain, from product creation and movement to customer response. This data forms the foundation of the Company’s AI and analytics capability. The Company’s approach is business-led and designed around reinforcing intelligence loops, not isolated point solutions.

Insights from trendspotting, demand sensing, buying, merchandising, supply chain, and customer engagement feed into one another, helping the business make faster, sharper, and more informed decisions. This capability was initially built through a central Centre of Excellence to create foundational tools, standards and reusable models. It is now being embedded deeper into the business, with data science teams working alongside designers, buyers, merchandisers and supply chain teams. This integration helps translate AI from prototypes into repeatable sources of advantage. Trent sees this work less as artificial intelligence and more as intelligence amplification. The aim is to enhance human judgement, instinct and expertise — not replace them. Technology extends the reach of people; the intelligence remains human, while the leverage becomes machine and the underlying AI models and tools.

During the year, the Company advanced AI-led interventions aligned to its strategic priorities of strengthening brands, deepening stores (and online in the case of Westside) and building a critical mass of presence in micro markets to drive awareness. This model facilitates a strong organic connection with our customers while at the same time affording better economics. Control over the value chain Our playbook involves complete ownership/ control over multiple parts of our value chain, from sourcing and production facilities to retailing. We believe many of these choices and disciplines (and in many respects counterintuitive at first instance) are integral to realising strong differentiation, agility, and relevance of the brands over time. Integrated back and differentiated front Trent has evolved into a platform with multiple retail brand propositions and the intent is to operate with a portfolio of growth engines (retail brands/ categories/ geographies).

We adopt a deeply differentiated approach to the customer-facing aspects of brands, and at the same time, a deeply integrated approach with respect to systems, processes, and infrastructure. Technology and supply chain investments Given the scale and the rapidly evolving consumer context, we are committing substantial investments in technology, automation, and the supply chain. We are increasingly leveraging multiple technology and AI interventions and starting to witness material outcomes. Structural cost management Structural cost management coupled with a focus on operating efficiencies is integral to our strategic priority of building resilience, particularly as we continue to scale in a dynamic operating environment. Our focus is on building an operating model that remains agile, disciplined, and adaptable across cycles.
